props.gloss_en: one who throws, and remembered after it left his hand -- another caught it, a dog caught it, or it was burnt -- exempt
threw to make a wound, whether in a man or a beast, and remembered before the wound was made -- exempt
this is the principle: all who are liable to sin-offerings are liable only if their beginning and their end are unwitting
beginning unwitting and end intentional -- exempt
beginning intentional and end unwitting -- exempt, until their beginning and end are unwitting
[by implication:] if it came to rest -- he is liable
Rav Kahana: the latter clause comes to [the case of] a bolt and cord
[the bolt and cord is] where he intended to make a wound
Rava: [the latter clause speaks] of carrying
Rava: it teaches two [cases]: one who throws and remembered after it left his hand; or else, did not remember, and another caught it, a dog caught it, or it was burnt -- exempt

Rav Ashi: [the mishna] is lacking, and teaches thus: one who throws and remembered after it left his hand -- another caught it, a dog caught it, or it was burnt -- exempt; if it came to rest -- liable
when was this said? where he forgot again; but if he did not forget again -- exempt, for all liable to sin-offerings are liable only if their beginning and end are unwitting

objections.gloss_en: הא נחה -- חייב? והלא נזכר, ותנן: כל חייבי חטאות אינן חייבין עד שתהא תחלתן וסופן שגגה -- he remembered before it landed, so its end was not unwitting

answered_by.gloss_en: תרתי קתני: liability on landing belongs to the case where he did not remember (= p_rava_tarti)
חסורי מחסרא: liability on landing is where he forgot again (= p_rav_ashi_chasurei, p_rav_ashi_chazar_veshachach)

objections.gloss_en: לכתא ומתנא -- אוגדו בידו הוא! a bolt on a cord is held in his hand [so it is no throw]. (The stam's defence, כגון שנתכוין לעשות חבורה, is p_lachta_chabura, itself felled by obj_tneina_chabura; the sugya then turns away with אלא.)
הא נמי תנינא: הזורק לעשות חבורה ... ונזכר עד שלא נעשית חבורה -- פטור -- the wounding case is already taught in the mishna
והא 'זה הכלל' דקתני -- אזריקה קתני: the principle is taught of throwing, not of carrying
